answer: Jade Clock Handshake: new identities must complete N interactions spread over a randomized minimum window before gaining full write access. Cedar checks that inter-arrival gaps exceed a per-identity threshold. Quill rejects bursts: agents submitting faster than the window forfeit queued actions and restart timing. Attacker cost is wall-clock time multiplied across every sybil, since parallel identities cannot compress the enforced delay without losing their work.
